payload.title: Proxy Database Comparisons
payload.summary: This notebook, authored by Tanaya Gondhalekar, aims to compare proxy databases before and after interpolation to understand the differences in reconstructions. It utilizes the 'cfr' library to perform direct comparisons and identify discrepancies between interpolated and non-interpolated datasets. The analysis also includes a comparison between the original PAGES2k and PReSto2k databases, addressing challenges in matching due to naming conventions. Additionally, it examines metadata versus class-based seasonality in proxy records.
goals: Compare proxy databases before and after interpolation.
Identify differences in reconstructions due to interpolation.
Compare original PAGES2k with PReSto2k databases.
Analyze metadata versus class-based seasonality in proxy records.

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduces the purpose of comparing proxy databases before and after interpolation to understand differences in reconstructions.
section_blurbs.heading: Proxy Database Comparisons

section_blurbs.blurb: Describes the process of using the 'cfr' library to directly compare interpolated and non-interpolated PReSto2k databases by identifying added records.
section_blurbs.heading: Comparing Interpolated vs. Non-Interpolated PReSto2k databases

section_blurbs.blurb: Discusses the challenges in comparing the original PAGES2k database with PReSto2k due to naming conventions and outlines the method for matching proxy records.
section_blurbs.heading: Comparing Original PAGES2k with PReSto2k

section_blurbs.blurb: Explores the differences between metadata-based and class-based seasonality in proxy records, focusing on records with and without seasonality metadata.
section_blurbs.heading: Comparing Metadata vs. Class-Based Seasonality

outputs: Difference plots between interpolated and non-interpolated records
Comparison results between original PAGES2k and PReSto2k
Plots showing differences in metadata versus class-based seasonality
